learning_outcomes.text: Provide students with the basis for the current assessment, verification and design of energy conversion systems, with particular reference to those most currently used in industrial plants.
Knowing and classifying the main and common energy systems, describing the operating principles of the various components.
Execute evaluations of system performance based on energy balances, taking into account the relative characteristics of machines and fluids.
Identify algorithmic approaches and to use databases to achieve the above training objectives.
Knowledge and understanding of thermodynamics applied to energy systems and of fluid-dynamic phenomena as well as models capable of representing them.
Knowledge of systems and machines for the production and conversion of energy, with particular reference to turbomachinery and industrial combustion equipment.
Understanding the role of different energy technologies in ensuring the environmental and economic sustainability of production.
Knowledge and understanding of information technology including the role they play in supporting design.
Understanding the organization of information in databases and computer design to support processes.

Applying knowledge and understanding related to analytical modelling and experimental methods to design, analyze and test fluid machines, thermal motors and energy conversion systems. This includes: the application of design criteria for technical and thermos-technical plants, fluid and energy distribution; the application of thermodynamic principles to simple systems; the understanding of the main thermodynamic cycles and the reading of thermal diagrams; the identification of significant heat transmission mechanisms for engineering applications; the analysis and functional design of equipment of mechanical interest such as turbomachinery, energy conversion systems and internal combustion engines; the evaluation of the energy, economic and environmental performance of fluid, thermal and oleo-dynamic machinery.
Graphic representation and communication (drafting of diagrams, graphs and tables)

Provide the student with an in-depth analysis on different topics related to Energy Engineering, like components design through advanced thermo-fluid-dynamics aspects and energy systems characterization, in the form of energy storage systems.
Provide the student with the knowledge and the methodologies necessary to face and solve, in a proper way, problems related to the treated aspects.
Knowledge and understanding of thermodynamics applied to energy systems and of fluid-dynamic phenomena as well as models capable of representing them.
Knowledge of systems and machines for the production and conversion of energy, with particular reference to turbomachinery and industrial combustion equipment.
Understanding the role of different energy technologies in ensuring the environmental and economic sustainability of production.

Applying knowledge and understanding related to analytical modelling and experimental methods to design, analyze and test fluid machines, thermal motors and energy conversion systems. This includes: the application of design criteria for technical and thermos-technical plants, fluid and energy distribution; the application of thermodynamic principles to simple systems; the understanding of the main thermodynamic cycles and the reading of thermal diagrams; the identification of significant heat transmission mechanisms for engineering applications; the analysis and functional design of equipment of mechanical interest such as turbomachinery, energy conversion systems and internal combustion engines; the evaluation of the energy, economic and environmental performance of fluid, thermal and oleo-dynamic machinery.
Graphic representation and communication (drafting of diagrams, graphs and tables)

Recognize and classify the main and most common energy systems, describe the operating principles of their various components, and carry out performance assessments of the plants based on energy balances, taking into account the relevant characteristics of the fluid machineries used.
Identify algorithmic approaches and use databases to achieve the aforementioned learning outcomes.
Apply the principles of thermodynamics to energy systems described by the main thermodynamic cycles.
Correctly interpret thermodynamic diagrams.
Select and apply appropriate analytical and modelling methods for thermal power plants and energy conversion systems.
Assess the energy and environmental performance of conversion plants.
Demonstrate communication skills through the graphical and tabular representation of thermodynamic cycles, systems and results.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate specific issues relating to energy systems clearly and rigorously, highlighting the criteria for analysis.
Develop models of energy conversion systems independently.
Practice and assess their ability to learn autonomously or with only partial guidance.
Gather further bibliographic information and develop the ability to solve problems and undertake simple projects.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to renewable Energy Systems and ORC
Energy Conversion national and worldwide scenario
Combustion Process: Fundamentals; specific applications for Energy Conversion plants
Steam PowerPlants: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Gas Turbine PowerPlants: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Reciprocating Internal Combustion Engine: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Combined Cycles and Cogeneration: thermodynamic features and components descriptions. Performance
Organic Rankine Cycles for Heat recovery at low temperature
Introduction to main energy systems for renewable energy sources exploitation
Examples of conventional and cooling system
Simplified design method for GT cooled components
CAES (Compressed Energy Storage Systems): principle, examples and efficiency improvement methods
Hydrogen-based energy storage: principle and comparison between methodologies
Energy system modeling systems using a modular object-oriented approach
Application to conventional and innovative systems
Numerical tools for modeling energy systems
teaching_methods: Group practice on assigned projects with periodic revisions

assessment_methods.method: Comprehensive written test (if mid-terms not passed)
Review and assessment of written assignment (Powerplants section)

assessment_rules: Students can pass by sitting two mid-term exams with an average mark of 10 or above, followed by an oral examination. If mid-term exams are not taken or passed, students must pass a comprehensive written test with a minimum mark of 14, followed by an oral exam. The written tests assess the ability to select and use mathematical models for thermodynamic analysis and cross-cutting competences, while the oral examination assesses the ability to describe energy systems and their components. For the 'PLANTS' section, the oral examination also includes a review and assessment of a written assignment.
